name: Jaasanja
title: Israelite who married a foreign woman
summary: Jaasanja (also known as Jaasu) is mentioned in the book of Ezra as one of the Israelites who had taken a foreign wife during the return from exile. He was among those required to separate from their foreign wives as part of Ezra's religious reforms to preserve the people's faithfulness to God.

keyEvents.title: Listed among those with foreign wives
keyEvents.description: Jaasanja is mentioned among the Israelites who had married foreign women, which was contrary to God's law.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's reforms
keyEvents.description: Ezra led a major reform movement in which Israelite men who had taken foreign wives were required to send them away to restore covenant faithfulness.

keyEvents.title: The people gather in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: All the men of Judah and Benjamin were summoned to Jerusalem within three days to address the issue of the foreign wives.

keyEvents.title: Agreement to send away the foreign wives
keyEvents.description: The people made a covenant to separate from their foreign wives and repent for their violation of God's law.
